provider: JFrog Artifactory Community Edition (CE for C/C++) / Artifactory OSS — self-hosted

free_tier.stated: Free of charge, self-hosted, no storage cap of any kind: the quota is whatever disk/object-store you attach. 'This product gives all the power and flexibility of the Artifactory repository for Conan and generic binaries to the C/C++ world completely free of charge.' OSS edition likewise downloadable and free.

egress.terms: Free by construction — you serve it from your own host/object store, so egress is your bill (or zero behind Cloudflare). Not a hosted egress concession.

interface_detail: rest (Artifactory REST API), plus every native protocol it supports: docker/OCI, maven, npm, pypi, nuget, generic, conan; JFrog CLI
tooling: JFrog CLI (`jf rt upload`), `curl -T` against the REST API, `oras`/`docker push` for OCI, and any package client. Real, first-party, actively maintained.
chaining: Not really chainable as free storage: each instance consumes your own disk. The only 'multiplier' is running it on someone else's free compute/disk, which is a different niche (IaaS), not an artifact-manager finding.
limits_note: CE for C/C++ is restricted to Conan + generic repository types only (no Docker/Maven/npm); OSS edition likewise feature-stripped. No HA, no S3 blob store on CE. Requires you to run Java + Postgres/derby and to pay for the bytes.
reliability_note: Mature, no data-vanishing risk; the catch is that 'free' means free software, not free storage — you are the storage provider.
confidence_note: One page read moves it to documented.
